scenes.vo: McDonald's pulled in nearly twenty six billion dollars last year — but less than half came from burgers.

visual.sub:
TOTAL REVENUE — LESS THAN HALF
FROM SELLING BURGERS

scenes.vo: Franchised restaurants brought in fifteen point seven billion — mostly rent and royalties, no matter the store's own profit.

items.text: McDonald's owns or leases the real estate
Franchisee pays rent + royalty, regardless of profit

scenes.vo: That's why McDonald's books a forty five percent operating margin — among the highest of any restaurant chain.

visual.sub:
OPERATING MARGIN — AMONG
THE HIGHEST IN RESTAURANTS

scenes.vo: McDonald's owns or leases the land and building, then re-leases it to the franchisee — collecting rent on top of royalties every month.

items.text: McDonald's owns or controls the real estate
Franchisee pays rent + royalty on sales

scenes.vo: Ninety five percent of McDonald's forty three thousand restaurants are franchised — McDonald's mostly collects the rent, not the orders.

visual.sub:
ARE FRANCHISED — McDONALD'S
MOSTLY COLLECTS THE RENT

scenes.vo: Every franchise agreement runs twenty years, and McDonald's holds the real estate the entire time — not the franchisee.

visual.sub:
McDONALD'S HOLDS THE REAL ESTATE —
NOT THE FRANCHISEE

scenes.vo: When a company owns the real estate under its franchisees, it isn't selling burgers — it's collecting rent, no matter who's behind the counter.

visual.display: When a company owns the *real* *estate* under its franchisees, it isn't selling burgers — it's collecting *rent,* no matter who's behind the counter.
